Volume 1 Hardware Fundamentals

Welcome to the Ultimate PC Building Guide (2026 Edition). Before touching a screwdriver, you must understand the anatomy of a PC.

What is a Computer?

At its core, a PC is a collection of specific components communicating over a main circuit board (the Motherboard). The CPU does the thinking, the RAM remembers what it's currently thinking about, the Storage (SSD/HDD) is the long-term memory, the GPU draws the pictures on your screen, and the Power Supply (PSU) gives them all electricity.

Storage Technologies

We have moved far beyond spinning hard drives (HDDs). Modern systems use NVMe SSDs that plug directly into the motherboard via PCIe lanes. PCIe Gen 4 can hit speeds of 7,000 MB/s, while PCIe Gen 5 pushes past 14,000 MB/s. Always install your OS on an NVMe SSD.

💡 Pro Tip: The RGB Ecosystem

RGB lighting looks great, but mixing brands (like Corsair fans with NZXT coolers) often requires installing multiple bloated software programs. Try to stick to one ecosystem if you want synchronized lighting.

Volume 2 Choosing Components

Step 1: Choose Your Budget

Your budget dictates your monitor resolution. ₹40,000 is great for 1080p Esports. ₹80,000 unlocks 1440p High settings. ₹1.5 Lakh+ pushes into 4K Ultra and AI workstation territory.

Step 2: Select the CPU

For gaming, single-core speed matters most (Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 is plenty). For heavy video editing, compiling code, or 3D rendering, core count matters (Core i9 / Ryzen 9).

Step 3: Motherboard Chipsets

Intel chipsets starting with 'Z' (Z790, Z890) allow CPU overclocking. 'B' series (B760) are for mainstream users who don't overclock. AMD uses 'X' (X670) for extreme enthusiasts and 'B' (B650) for mainstream. Ensure the socket matches your CPU.

Step 4: RAM (Memory)

32GB is the new standard for 2026. If using DDR5, aim for 6000MHz speed as the sweet spot for stability and performance. Always buy RAM in pairs (e.g., 2x16GB) to run in Dual Channel mode, which doubles your bandwidth.

Volume 5 Building the PC

Step 1: Prepare Workspace

Clear a large table. Do not build on carpet to avoid static electricity. Take your motherboard out and place it on top of its cardboard box. This is your test bench.

Step 2: Install CPU

Lift the retention arm. Line up the golden triangle on the bottom corner of the CPU with the triangle on the motherboard socket. Gently drop it in. Do not push. Lock the arm back down.

Step 3: Install RAM

Check your motherboard manual (usually slots 2 and 4 are filled first). Push the RAM stick straight down until you hear a loud CLICK from both sides.

🚨 Safety First: Stand-offs

When moving the motherboard into the PC case (Step 7), ensure the metal stand-offs in the case align perfectly with the holes in the motherboard. A misplaced stand-off can short-circuit the board!

Volume 19 Recommended Builds

1. The Budget Gamer (₹60k - ₹80k)

Target: 1080p High FPS Gaming.
Recommended: Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5, 16GB DDR4, 1TB NVMe, RTX 4060 or RX 7600.

2. The Creator Workstation (₹1.5L - ₹3L)

Target: 4K Video Editing, 3D Rendering.
Recommended: Intel Core i9 / Ryzen 9, 64GB DDR5, 4TB Gen4 NVMe, RTX 4080 SUPER.

3. AI Workstation (RTX 50-Series Class)

Target: Local LLMs, Stable Diffusion.
Recommended: VRAM is king here. Aim for RTX 4090 (24GB VRAM) or multiple high-VRAM cards, 128GB DDR5 System RAM, 1000W+ Platinum PSU.
